profiles.meeting_scenario: An asset-management firm is holding a design review for a proposal to add a new model aggregation (MA) approach for portfolio risk evaluation into its portfolio construction platform. The context is an upcoming pilot for a large pension client that wants more robust portfolio optimization under distributional uncertainty, while the firm also wants to preserve compatibility with its existing VaR/ES reporting process. The agenda is to review whether the proposed MA design is suitable for the pilot, whether its Wasserstein and mean-variance formulations fit the firm's current risk infrastructure, and what modifications are needed before approval. The expected outcome is a decision on whether to move the design forward for the pilot and what implementation assumptions the team will carry into the next draft.

members.name: Ethan Rao
members.expertise: robust optimization, portfolio risk models, convex reformulations
members.background: Ethan leads the firm's quantitative research group and has spent the last six months adapting recent stochastic-dominance and distributionally robust optimization methods for internal portfolio tools; he is comfortable moving from academic formulations to prototype implementations.
members.private_state: He wants the review to confirm that the MA approach is technically sound enough to proceed without reopening the mathematical design, and he is trying to avoid expanding the first implementation into a broader platform integration effort.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the MA approach yields a 'robust distribution,' they mean a canonical loss distribution that can become the primary downstream object for computing any risk measure later.
When colleagues refer to the 'mean-variance uncertainty set,' they are naturally referring to the research library's quarterly calibrated ambiguity set used in his benchmark studies.
In a design review for a pilot, 'ready' mainly means the formulation is mathematically validated, reproducible on benchmark portfolios, and fast enough for the overnight batch window.

Saying the design can 'fit the existing optimizer' means swapping the risk-evaluation module inside the current strategic allocation workflow, not revalidating every production mandate constraint and cost hook.
If governance or reporting teams need extra artifacts, those can be layered on after the core design is approved rather than being part of design completeness.

members.name: Laura Chen
members.expertise: risk system integration, model governance, institutional client rollout
members.background: Laura oversees the production risk and optimization platform used by portfolio managers and client-reporting teams; she routinely translates quantitative methods into approved operational workflows that can pass governance and client scrutiny.
members.private_state: She wants the new method to look like a clean extension of the firm's current risk stack so the pension-client pilot can proceed without triggering a separate model-governance escalation or workflow rewrite.
hidden_assumptions: A 'robust distribution' is an explanatory distributional output that supplements current official scenario engines and reports, not a replacement source for downstream controls.
The 'mean-variance uncertainty set' means the production-approved market-risk guardrail configuration already recognized by treasury and model governance.
For a pilot, 'ready' includes client-facing explainability, lineage logging, and parity checks against current VaR/ES outputs, not just mathematical correctness and runtime.
If a design is said to use the 'existing optimizer,' that includes the full production optimization service with mandate constraints, turnover rules, and transaction-cost hooks already wired in.
Anything shown to a real client is effectively part of the governed production path, even if researchers still think of it as a prototype.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both participants talk positively about the MA approach producing a 'robust distribution.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a single canonical loss distribution that will serve as the main downstream object from which VaR, ES, and other risk measures can all be computed.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means an additional distributional summary used for explanation and reporting, while the existing official scenario engine remains the operational source for downstream controls.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds inherently beneficial to both sides, and each person hears their own familiar interpretation of what extra distributional output should do; because neither is contesting the value of the output, they do not think to define its status in the architecture.

misalignment_points.topic: Which mean-variance uncertainty set is being reused
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to begin with 'the mean-variance set we already use' before expanding to other uncertainty sets.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the quant research group's quarterly calibrated ambiguity-set template used in internal notebooks and benchmark experiments.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the production 'MV guardrail' parameter set already approved by treasury and model governance for portfolio oversight.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The two artifacts have similar names, both are internal, and both are associated with mean/variance ambiguity, so the shorthand feels precise enough in conversation even though they point to different parameterizations and governance histories.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the design should be 'pilot-ready' after the next iteration.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the method reproduces benchmark results, has a stable convex reformulation, and completes within the overnight runtime budget on representative portfolios.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means it also has explainability notes, lineage logging, and comparison outputs showing how MA relates to current VaR/ES reporting for client and governance review.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Design reviews often compress multiple readiness dimensions into one phrase, and each participant assumes the other naturally includes the standards normal for their own function; because they both expect the other to be competent, the mismatch remains invisible.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the MA approach can be integrated by 'using the existing optimizer' without a major rewrite.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means replacing only the risk-evaluation component in the strategic allocation flow and testing on simplified portfolio constraints similar to the research examples.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the method will run inside the full production optimizer service with existing mandate rules, turnover penalties, and transaction-cost hooks left intact.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: At the surface level both are reassuring each other that no new optimizer needs to be built, so the phrase conveys efficiency and compatibility; the missing detail is not the optimizer itself but the assumed boundary of what parts of the production wrapper come along with it.
